summary: Phase A closed for engine-score. I wrote the whole test list J (8 files, 111 tests in src/engine/score/*.test.ts) on top of the existing engine. Where a test found a real bug I fixed the engine instead of weakening the test. (1) Waltz meter and downbeat failed on some streams: the global 10th-percentile 'bass' mistook the waltz chords for bass. Bass is now relative to the lowest pitch within +-2 beats. (2) Fast sparse melodies (>150 bpm, bass on beats 1 and 3) were read at half speed (off-beat threshold SUB_FREE raised from 1.8 to 2.0). A sweep of 8 928 synthetic streams (4 styles, 60-180 bpm, +-15 ms jitter, pickups, 8-16 bars) now gives 0 tempo (3 %), key, meter or downbeat errors (before: 23 tempo and 186 meter/downbeat errors). The 10 ground-truth fixtures in test/fixtures also come out right. (3) Chords with two notes on one letter and octave (B + B# in D# minor, F + F# in C) broke abcjs ties and playback. The new spellChord respells them (notes always climb the staff, with the fewest accidentals); the ABC and MusicXML writers use it. (4) When a tie carried over the barline was split again inside the bar, the continuation printed an accidental. Tie continuations now never print one, a carried accidental is restated for later notes, and the key-signature pitch gets a courtesy accidental. (5) In 'facil', the left hand rested as soon as the bass note stopped sounding. The bass is now held to the next bass note (at most to the end of its bar unless it is still sounding, and restruck every bar). Note names (client feedback, Avance 2): scoreToAbc now emits %%annotationfont at 8 pt = 11 px in the app font. The abcjs default is 12 pt = 16 px, so names are 67 % of the old size. abcjs applies it (checked in its formatting and in the 11px rendered font-size). Lead request: in sixteenth-note beats only the first new note of the beat is named, so the Prelude reads 'Mi Mi Mi Mi' instead of 'Mi SolDoMi SolDoMi'. I checked the demos bar by bar in abcjs, light and dark. The Ode and the Minuet match their texts with exact rhythms. The Prelude's split point moved from 65 to 62 because 65 fragmented bar 8. Also added: suggestMeasuresPerLine, spellChord, findDemo/DEMO_ID_PREFIX, and harness fixes.

public_api_notes:
IMPORTS: only from 'src/engine/score' (index.ts); demos from 'src/data/demos'. Everything is pure TS, deterministic and never throws.
PIPELINE: analyzeNotes(notes) -> defaultParams(analysis, {quantize, splitPoint, defaultDifficulty}) -> buildScore(notes, params, analysis, title?) -> summarizeScore(score). analyzeNotes returns an integer bpm (50..200), beatOffset = seconds of the first downbeat in the source audio, and '4/4' or '3/4' ('6/8' is never automatic). Empty input -> {bpm 100, beatOffset 0, '4/4', C major, confidences 0}. About 25 ms for 1 900 notes. defaultParams: key null (= analysed key), transpose 0, minVelocity 0.1, minDuration 0.05 s, pitchRange [21,108], maxPolyphony 4. sanitizeParams(partial, analysis?) repairs stored or edited params. buildScore takes 4.5-6 ms for 3 000 notes (budget 30 ms): rebuild on every change and debounce only the DB writes.
TIME: 1 tick = one sixteenth (TICKS_PER_QUARTER 4). ticksPerMeasureOf: 4/4 16, 3/4 12, 2/4 8, 6/8 12; beatTicksOf: 4 (6 in 6/8). ScoreEvent.start is relative to its measure: absolute tick = measure.index * score.ticksPerMeasure + event.start. tickToSeconds(score, absTick) = absTick * 60 / bpm / 4 = seconds from tick 0 of measure 0. Also secondsToTick (fractional inverse), secondsPerTick(score) and measureDurationSeconds(score); score.durationSeconds = measureCount * measure duration. Source-audio time = score.startSeconds + tickToSeconds(score, tick). startSeconds is params.beatOffset shifted by whole measures so the first note lands in measure 0. With a pickup the score starts one bar before the first downbeat, and startSeconds CAN BE NEGATIVE (the score begins before the audio). abcjs synth time t (at 100 % speed) maps to tick t / secondsPerTick(score).
SCORE: staves = [right/treble, left/bass], always both, same measureCount >= 1, trailing empty bars trimmed. Each measure's events tile [0, ticksPerMeasure) exactly; a rest has pitches []; pitches are ascending. tie: true = every pitch continues into the next event of the same staff (also across the barline). stats: noteCount (tied pieces counted once), maxPolyphony, range [lo,hi] | null, notesPerSecond, difficulty 1|2|3 -> DIFFICULTY_LABELS. Labels for params.difficulty: DIFFICULTY_PARAM_LABELS. TIME_SIGNATURES = ['4/4','3/4','2/4','6/8']. All Score pitches stay within 21..108 (transposition folds by octaves), so ABC from scoreToAbc needs no extra clamping to SOUNDFONT_PITCH_RANGE (21..109).
PARAMS: score.key = transposeKey(params.key ?? analysis.key, params.transpose), already transposed, so display keyName(score.key, naming). pitchRange filters RAW (untransposed) pitches. minDuration is in seconds, minVelocity in 0..1. maxPolyphony is per hand per onset, 1..6 (keeps the outer voices, then the loudest). quantize is 8|16 (intermedio and facil always use the 8th grid). splitPoint: pitch >= splitPoint goes right; a chord straddling it by <= 2 semitones stays in its majority hand. difficulty: original | intermedio (8th grid, <= 3 notes per hand, ghost notes of big chords dropped) | facil (right-hand top line; left hand one bass note per beat, held to the next bass note or the end of the bar). One chord stream per staff: a note still sounding when its hand plays again is cut at that onset.
ABC: scoreToAbc(score, {hands?: 'both'|'right'|'left', noteNaming?: 'none'|'latin'|'english', includeTitle?: false, measuresPerLine?: 4, printTempo?: true, annotationSize?: 8, annotationFont?: app font, nameEveryNote?: false}). Output: X:1, [T:], M:, L:1/16, [%%printtempo false], Q:1/4=bpm (6/8: Q:3/8=round(bpm/1.5)), [%%annotationfont "<font>" 8, only with names], %%score {RH | LH} (both hands: brace and connected barlines), V:RH clef=treble, V:LH clef=bass, K:, %%MIDI program 0, then one [V:RH] line and one [V:LH] line per system, ending with |]. hands 'right'/'left' emit only that voice (display AND playback). tune.lines[i].staff[0] = RH, staff[1] = LH. Accidentals are key-aware and last to the end of the bar per letter and octave (the abcjs rule); naturals cancel them; a courtesy accidental follows a tie over the barline. Checked with abcjs's own parser and playback flattener (tune.setUpAudio) on 1 500 random scores: no warnings, and abcjs plays exactly the Score's notes.
NOTE NAMES (the rule the viewer layout should match): abcjs 'below' annotations, class abcjs-annotation (with add_classes), 8 pt = 11 px, app font. Chords: up to 3 stacked names (highest first); bigger chords show only the outer two. Tie continuations get no name. Thinning: in a beat (a quarter, or a dotted quarter in 6/8) where a new note starts on a sixteenth position (odd tick), or that holds more new notes than eighths fit, only the beat's first new note is named. Eighths and slower keep every name. nameEveryNote: true turns thinning off. namedEvents is internal; layout code should use suggestMeasuresPerLine.
LAYOUT: suggestMeasuresPerLine(score, staffwidth, {noteNames?, zoom?, nameEveryNote?}) returns 1..8 bars per system. It budgets 16 units per event + 6 per drawn name + 10 per bar (busier staff, 90th-percentile bar) after 40 units for clef and key. staffwidth is in abcjs units (about CSS px at zoom 1). Demos at 330 with names: Ode 2, Minuet 2, Prelude 1; Ode at 440 -> 3. After the thinning, the Prelude also reads well at 2 bars per line on 390 px (see the screenshot). abcjs gotchas found here: (1) responsive: 'resize' turns the render target into an aspect-ratio box (padding-bottom %, overflow hidden), so render into an element WITHOUT padding (pad a wrapper), or the bottom of the score is clipped. (2) abcjs reserves no horizontal room for annotations: use paddingright ~10 so the last name of a line is not cut. (3) Quieter names: .abcjs-annotation { fill: var(--ink-2) } (used in the harness, legible in light and dark).
EXPORTS: scoreToMusicXml(score): string (MusicXML 4.0 partwise, divisions 4; '.musicxml', 'application/vnd.recordare.musicxml+xml'). scoreToMidi(score): Uint8Array ('.mid', 'audio/midi'; tracks MIDI_TRACK_NAMES ['Mano derecha','Mano izquierda'], program 0, channels 0/1, ties merged, no key-signature meta event; about 85 ms for 150 bars). ABC file: scoreToAbc(score, {includeTitle: true}) with noteNaming 'none' ('.abc', 'text/vnd.abc').
NAMES AND KEYS: keyName(key, naming) -> 'Sol mayor' / 'G mayor' ('none' behaves like latin). pitchName(midi, naming, key?) -> 'Do4' / 'C4' (C4 = 60, spelled in the key). pitchClassName(midi, naming, key?) -> 'Fa#'. transposeKey(key, semis) picks fewer accidentals; 6-accidental ties keep the original key's side. allKeys() = 24 keys for the key picker (majors Db..F#, then minors Eb..G#, in fifths order). Also keyFromFifths, keyFromPc, normalizeKey, tonicPc, spellPitch(midi, key) -> {step, alter, octave}, spellChord(ascending pitches, key), emptyAnalysis, NOTE_VALUES, meterParts, isTimeSignature, splitDuration.
DEMOS (src/data/demos.ts): demoPieces = [{slug, title, composer, bpm, timeSignature, notes, key, splitPoint}]: 'oda-alegria' (L. van Beethoven, 4/4, 100 bpm, G major, split 60, 16 bars, 38.4 s), 'minueto-sol' (C. Petzold, 3/4, 112 bpm, G major, split 64, 16 bars, 25.7 s), 'preludio-do' (J. S. Bach, 4/4, 66 bpm, C major, split 62, 8 bars, 29.1 s). Library ids = DEMO_ID_PREFIX + slug ('demo-oda-alegria'); findDemo(idOrSlug) finds a demo by id or slug. SEED WITH analysis = demoAnalysis(demo) (detected analysis pinned to the known bpm, meter and key, beatOffset 0, confidences 1) and params = { ...demoParams(demo, getSettings()), difficulty: 'original' }. demoParams is defaultParams plus the demo's splitPoint. Plain defaultParams with the usual split 60 puts the Prelude's bass (C4) and the Minuet's D4 on the treble staff. durationSec = buildScore(...).durationSeconds.

requests.request: seed.ts: build each demo with demoAnalysis(demo) and { ...demoParams(demo, getSettings()), difficulty: 'original' } (this keeps the per-demo splitPoint 60/64/62). id = DEMO_ID_PREFIX + slug; durationSec = buildScore(...).durationSeconds; summary = summarizeScore(score).

abcjs render: with responsive 'resize', render into a padding-free element (put the paper padding on a wrapper); otherwise the bottom of the score is clipped. Use paddingright ~10 so the last note name of a line is not cut. Optionally .abcjs-annotation { fill: var(--ink-2) } for quieter names (verified in light and dark in test/harness/abc.html).

measuresPerLine: use suggestMeasuresPerLine(score, staffwidth, { noteNames: naming !== 'none', zoom }), or a rule matching the documented name thinning (one name per sixteenth-note beat). At staffwidth 330 it gives 1 bar per line for the Prelude and 2 for the Ode and Minuet.

'Restablecer' in the Filters tab: for demo items use findDemo(doc.id) ? demoParams(demo, settings) : defaultParams(doc.analysis, settings), so demos keep their split point. For 'Original' playback, score.startSeconds can be negative (the score starts before the audio). ABC export: scoreToAbc(score, { includeTitle: true }) with noteNaming 'none'.

docs/CONTINUAR.md sections 4 and 7: engine-score is closed (tests written, note names shrunk and thinned, demos checked). The note-names-too-big item is done; docs/screenshots/engine-score-nombres-antes-ahora.png shows before and after.

known_issues: Tempo octave ambiguity is inherent and remains. Continuous-eighth textures (Alberti bass, left-hand arpeggios with flat velocities) below ~100 bpm can be detected at double tempo, and sparse fast melodies with heavy timing jitter (+-25 ms) at half tempo. The Prelude demo analyses as 132 bpm instead of 66; demos pin their tempo, so users never see this. Users can correct the tempo with 'Tempo base'.

One chord stream per staff (no second voice): a note still sounding when the same hand plays again is cut at that onset. For example, a held bass under a moving line on the same staff becomes a short note.

The hand split is one split point plus a small chord heuristic. No single split point reproduces Bach's hands in the Prelude, so in bars 1-7 the second note of each figure sits on the upper staff (Bach writes it in the left hand). Bar 8 is exactly as written.
abcjs reserves no horizontal room for annotations. Names are thinned in sixteenth-note beats, but long names (Fa#, Sol) can still touch in eighth-note passages squeezed into narrow lines.
The MIDI export has no key-signature meta event (@tonejs/midi 2.0 encodes it incorrectly) and takes ~85 ms for 150 bars (a one-off export).
Courtesy accidentals appear only after ties over the barline; there are no cautionary accidentals in the bar after an altered note.
6/8 is never detected automatically (by design; it is a user choice).
verification: npx vitest run: 12 files, 148 tests passed. engine-score: 8 files, 111 tests (spelling 21, durations 6, build 32, analysis 7, abc 21, musicxml 7, midi 4, demos 13). They cover: spelling in all 30 key signatures, bar accidental state, duration decomposition for every span of every meter, barline ties, equal staves, empty and garbage input, filters and transposition, all difficulty modes, analysis accuracy at 60-180 bpm with +-15 ms jitter (within 3 %) and keys for all 24 major/minor keys, performance (median < 30 ms for 3 000 notes), abcjs.parseOnly without warnings and abcjs playback equal to the score notes, MusicXML well-formed (python xml.dom.minidom) with exact per-measure durations and notes, MIDI round-trip with @tonejs/midi, and clean demos. npx tsc --noEmit: 0 errors (whole project); with --noUnusedLocals --noUnusedParameters, no findings in my files. Extra sweeps in my temp folder (not in the suite): 8 928 synthetic streams -> 0 tempo/key/meter/downbeat errors; ground-truth JSON of the 10 test/fixtures -> bpm, downbeat and key right; abcjs oracle on 1 500 random scores -> 0 warnings and 0 note mismatches. Timings: buildScore 4.5-5.9 ms per 3 000 notes; analyzeNotes 24 ms for 1 881 notes; scoreToAbc 5 ms, MusicXML 9 ms and MIDI 85 ms for 151 bars. Visual check: node scripts/serve.mjs start 5183, then test/harness/abc.html with the 3 demos plus the stress and 6/8 cases, light and dark; I looked at every screenshot with Read. After the name thinning I also checked the Prelude at 2 bars per line on 390 px. node scripts/serve.mjs stop 5183 done (nothing listens on 5183).
